summary: The request's premise is half true. `parrot agent` is NOT a print()-based console — it already uses Rich end to end (banner, errors, tables, markdown, tool panels, usage) and prompt_toolkit for input; there are zero print() calls in packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/cli. The real defect is one function: ResponseRenderer.render_stream_chunk() writes raw sys.stdout.write(text), and because REPLConfig.streaming defaults to True that raw path is what every user sees by default. The good Markdown renderer is reachable only via --no-stream. The documented reason for the raw write is a genuine conflict between rich.live.Live and prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout() — but the sibling command `parrot devloop` already solved that exact conflict in the same package with a modal pause/resume discipline. So this is a homologation feature (bring `parrot agent` up to the standard `parrot devloop` already set), not a greenfield TUI adoption. Rich, prompt_toolkit and questionary are already core dependencies; InquirerPy would duplicate questionary, which is already what `parrot agent`'s own agent picker uses; Textual appears in no pyproject in the repo and would be the only genuinely new dependency. Note: HEAD advanced by two commits (3b5e4fed5, 7c2790044) during this research run, both on this surface. Neither touched the raw write; each added another compensating layer (_BlockingSafeFile write-retry, _mute_stream_loggers log suppression), bringing the count of stacked workarounds around this one seam to three. All line references in this synthesis are against the post-commit HEAD.

WORKAROUND #2 (added mid-research) — retries writes that BlockingIOError because patch_stdout() makes the fd non-blocking
WORKAROUND #3 (added mid-research) — silences console log handlers during a stream so log lines stop interleaving with tokens

REFERENCE — the working Live-under-patch_stdout pattern to homologate

BLAST RADIUS — second consumer, monkeypatches around the missing post-turn hook

specified as generic and reusable (devloop spec G2) — reuse candidate

constraints.statement: rich.live.Live emits cursor-control ANSI (\x1b[2K, \x1b[?25l) that prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout()'s StdoutProxy mangles into literal '?[2K'; every Console in the CLI already works around this with file=sys.__stdout__, force_terminal=True.
The conflict is solvable under prompt_toolkit: devloop runs Live and prompt_async together by pausing the Live region around every prompt ('one writer at a time').
rich>=13.0, prompt_toolkit>=3.0 and questionary>=2.1.1 are already core dependencies of ai-parrot; adding InquirerPy would duplicate questionary's role.
Textual appears in zero .toml files in the repository — it is a new dependency, not an activation of an existing one.
Rich is already established across 30 files in 4 distributions, so a Rich-based refactor extends an existing convention.
AgentREPL/ResponseRenderer/REPLConfig are imported cross-package by ai-parrot-integrations' agentd CLI; their constructor signatures are a de-facto public API.
AgentREPL.run() exposes no post-turn hook, forcing agentd to shadow send/send_stream at the instance level — a documented workaround this refactor could retire.
Three separate Console instances exist (agent_repl.py:25, repl.py:95, renderer.py:42) with no shared configuration point for theme/width/record.

tests/cli/test_integration.py (FEAT-168) is mock-based and covers the renderer, both send paths, slash commands and the Click command; devloop has its own console/renderer suite that models how to test a Live console.
RunView is coupled to dev-loop SessionHost envelope semantics (replay_since, gate handlers) and cannot be instantiated by the agent REPL as-is — it is a pattern, not a reusable class.

Three stacked workarounds now compensate for the same unaddressed seam: Console(file=sys.__stdout__) proxy bypass, _BlockingSafeFile write-retry, and _mute_stream_loggers log suppression during streams. Two of the three landed on 2026-09-02 while this research ran, and neither touched render_stream_chunk.
Log lines interleaving with streamed tokens is an additional symptom of streaming outside a managed render region; it was not named in the original request but is now being worked around in code.

hypotheses.statement: The perceived 'poor and cheap' look & feel is caused almost entirely by ResponseRenderer.render_stream_chunk()'s raw sys.stdout.write on the default streaming path, which discards Markdown, syntax highlighting and wrapping that the batch path already provides. Restoring rendered output to the streaming path — by adopting devloop's modal pause/resume Live discipline, or at minimum re-rendering the accumulated buffer as Markdown at stream end — addresses the complaint without any new dependency.
hypotheses.reasoning: The batch path already renders Markdown/panels/tables, streaming defaults to True, and the one raw write sits exactly on that default path.

hypotheses.statement: The secondary cause is architectural: AgentREPL.run() is a monolithic loop with no rendering-strategy seam and no post-turn hook, so neither the agent console nor agentd can vary presentation without monkeypatching. Extracting a console/renderer seam is what makes further UX work (and devloop homologation) cheap.
hypotheses.reasoning: agentd's own docstring names the missing post-turn hook; three unshared Console instances show no central presentation layer; and F011 shows two further workarounds accreted on this seam during the research run itself rather than a fix at the source.

hypotheses.statement: [REJECTED by U1] A full Textual TUI would dissolve the Live-vs-patch_stdout conflict outright by owning the screen (no prompt_toolkit patching, native scrollback, a real Markdown widget), but it is a new dependency, a rewrite of the input layer, incompatible with piping/non-TTY use, and would fork the agent console away from devloop's Rich conventions rather than homologating with them.
hypotheses.reasoning: Textual is absent from every pyproject while Rich spans 30 files; the conflict it would solve is already solved in-repo by cheaper means.

scope.statement: Extract a shared Rich console/presentation layer for the parrot CLI and migrate `parrot agent` onto it, adopting devloop's modal pause/resume Live discipline so streamed responses render with the same fidelity as batch responses. Keep prompt_toolkit and questionary; adopt neither Textual nor InquirerPy. Bring `parrot attach` (agentd) onto the same layer and give AgentREPL a real post-turn hook so its monkeypatch can be retired. Retire the three stacked workarounds (sys.__stdout__ bypass, _BlockingSafeFile, _mute_stream_loggers) as the seam makes them unnecessary.
out_of_scope: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/cli/tool_worker.py (its sys.stdout.write is an IPC marker protocol, not display)

unknowns.question: Which architecture: an inline-console upgrade (Rich Live + devloop's pause/resume discipline, keeping prompt_toolkit) or a full-screen Textual app with its own scrolling chat area and Markdown widget?
unknowns.why: The source explicitly left this open ('or Textual'). It decides dependency footprint, whether piping still works, and whether the agent console converges with or forks from devloop.
unknowns.user_answer: Inline Rich + pause/resume. Keep prompt_toolkit and adopt devloop's modal 'one writer at a time' Live discipline so streamed tokens render as Markdown in a Live region that pauses around every prompt. No new dependencies; converges with devloop; piping/non-TTY preserved; the three stacked workarounds become removable. Textual is explicitly NOT adopted.

unknowns.question: Is InquirerPy a hard requirement, or is questionary (already a core dependency, already used by parrot agent's own picker) acceptable for confirmations and HITL?
unknowns.why: Both wrap prompt_toolkit and cover the same role; adopting InquirerPy adds a redundant dependency to core.
unknowns.user_answer: Keep questionary (already core >=2.1.1, already powers parrot agent's own picker at loaders.py:103-120). InquirerPy is explicitly NOT adopted.

unknowns.question: Should the refactor extract a shared console/presentation layer used by parrot agent, parrot devloop and parrot attach, or stay local to parrot agent?
unknowns.why: Determines whether this is a contained fix or a cross-package refactor with a de-facto public API change.
unknowns.user_answer: Extract a shared console/presentation layer used by parrot agent, parrot devloop and parrot attach — single Console, one Live discipline, pluggable renderer. Cross-package refactor, accepted.

unknowns.question: Should this feature also give AgentREPL a real post-turn hook so agentd can retire its send/send_stream monkeypatch?
unknowns.why: agentd's own docstring flags this as deferred scope; doing it here is cheap, doing it later means touching the same seam twice.
unknowns.user_answer: Yes — give AgentREPL a real post-turn hook and retire agentd's send/send_stream instance-level monkeypatch.

recommended_next_command.rationale: All four unknowns are resolved, localization is high-confidence and verified against post-commit HEAD, and the architectural fork the source left open (inline Rich vs Textual) is now decided in favour of inline Rich + pause/resume. Nothing remains that options analysis would settle, so /sdd-brainstorm is no longer warranted.
